standard.title: Grammatical structures and basic syntax
standard.description: recognise target language conventions, grammatical structures and basic syntax in familiar texts and contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students recognise grammatical agreement markers, basic word class features, simple verb forms, affirmative and negative statements (AC9LS2U02). They have not yet worked with plural agreement, expanded possessives, a range of prepositions, question words, or the distinction between different forms of key verbs.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and use target language grammatical structures and basic syntax — including agreement patterns, pronouns, possessives, verb forms, prepositions, conjunctions and adverbs in familiar contexts.

nodes.label: Agreement patterns and possessives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply agreement patterns in singular and plural forms and use possessive markers in familiar sentence contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least two plural word groups with correct agreement; use at least three different possessive forms correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Apply agreement patterns across singular and plural forms; use personal pronouns with attention to subject omission patterns; use possessive markers in varied forms; identify word class items that do not follow regular patterns.
wider: Produce a short paragraph using at least five different pronouns and three possessive forms correctly — demonstrating range across the system
Find target language words that do not follow the regular agreement pattern and explain how their class is signalled in context
nodes.hinge_reason: Agreement patterns in plural and possessive forms are core grammatical systems governing all noun-phrase and sentence production. Students with inconsistent agreement produce systematic errors throughout all sentence-level work.

response_modes.reason: Agreement accuracy requires repeated production practice across varied conditions. Students who understand the rule intellectually still make agreement errors under production pressure.

success_criteria: Produces correct agreement in at least two plural word groups
Uses at least three different possessive forms correctly in context

nodes.label: Verb forms, prepositions and time adverbs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use common verbs in familiar forms, prepositions for location and direction, and time adverbs in modelled sentence contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least three different verbs correctly in familiar forms; use at least one preposition for location; use at least one time adverb.
nodes.typical_width: Use common verbs in familiar first and third person forms; use a range of prepositions for location and direction; use time adverbs and day/time expressions; use adjectives for description; apply key verb distinctions (e.g. where the target language distinguishes concepts that English expresses with a single verb).
wider: Produce a short paragraph describing a routine using at least three different verbs, two prepositions and two time adverbs correctly
Produce paired sentences demonstrating a key verb distinction in the target language — and explain the difference in English

response_modes.reason: Verb, preposition and adverb range develops through varied meaning-making contexts. Students who practise these only in isolated drills do not develop the flexible application needed for text production.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Key verb distinctions in the target language are among the most productive areas of grammatical depth — particularly where they encode concepts English treats as a single word. Width investment here builds understanding that pays dividends across all subsequent bands.
success_criteria: Uses at least three different verbs correctly in familiar sentence contexts
Uses at least one preposition and one time adverb correctly in connected sentences

nodes.label: Conjunctions, question words and imperatives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can link ideas using conjunctions, use question words in modelled structures, and apply imperative forms in familiar contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Link at least two ideas using conjunctions; use at least one question word in a modelled structure; use at least one imperative form.
nodes.typical_width: Link ideas with a range of conjunctions including contrast and addition; use question words to seek varied types of information; use and respond to imperatives; apply punctuation and capitalisation conventions; use number expressions for time, dates and quantities.
wider: Write connected sentences using a different conjunction in each — demonstrating range across the connective repertoire
Produce a question for each of the main question words studied — demonstrating that question word choice matches the information sought

response_modes.reason: Conjunction and question word range develops through accumulating examples across varied contexts. Students need to encounter each form in multiple meaningful uses before distinctions become reliable.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Conjunctions and question words are the grammatical tools that enable genuinely connected discourse — not just sentences in sequence. Width investment here builds the connective repertoire that underpins all extended language production.
success_criteria: Links at least two ideas using conjunctions correctly
Uses at least one question word correctly in a modelled question structure
